reforms.description: The System of Subsidies for Promoting the Development of Computers was adopted, providing conditional loans for the development costs of new machines to boost the domestic computer industry.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By providing financial support for computer technology development, the reform is expected to stimulate innovation and enhance competitiveness in the tech sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The system has been adopted but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform is significant as it provides targeted funding to support a key area of technological advancement.
reforms.source_quote: In 1971, the System of Subsidies for Promoting the Development of Computers was adopted: a 50 percent conditional loan was provided for the development costs of the new machines.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform involves a 'System of Subsidies for Promoting the Development of Computers' providing conditional loans for development costs, which qualifies as an innovation instrument for firms.

reforms.description: Japan established the Very Large Scale Integrated (VLSI) circuit research association under MITI in 1976, pooling R&D efforts of major semiconductor producers on basic technology with government co-financing of approximately 40% of total R&D costs over the four-year period (FY 1976–1979). This was a major public-private collaborative initiative to advance semiconductor technology.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Co-financed basic research in semiconductors aimed to build technological capability in a strategic, high-value sector, supporting long-term productivity and competitiveness.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states the association was established and operated over FY 1976–1979 with government co-financing.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural public-private research programme with significant government co-financing (40%) targeting a strategic technology sector; major initiative for the period.
reforms.source_quote: An important factor in the early development of the semi-conductor industry was the Very Large Scale Integrated circuit (VLSI) research association, sponsored by MITI under the Mining and Manufacturing Industry Technological Research Association Law... the total R&D cost over the four-year period the scheme was in operation (FY 1976 to FY 1979 inclusive) was about 75 billion yen, about two-fifths of which was financed by the Government.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The establishment of the VLSI circuit research association involved government co-financing of R&D costs, indicating direct public R&D funding for semiconductor technology.

reforms.description: Japan adopted the System of Subsidies for Promoting the Development of Computers in 1971, providing 50% conditional loans for development costs of new computer machines to support domestic producers in competing with Western firms.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Direct subsidies for applied R&D in computers aimed to build domestic industrial capability in a strategic, high-technology sector, supporting competitiveness and long-term productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states the system was adopted in 1971 and provided subsidies to domestic producers.
reforms.importance_rationale: Major sectoral R&D support programme with substantial subsidy rate (50% of development costs) targeting a strategic technology sector.
reforms.source_quote: In 1971, the System of Subsidies for Promoting the Development of Computers was adopted: a 50 per cent conditional loan was provided for the development costs of the new machines.
reforms.cross_verification_note: This reform describes the 'System of Subsidies for Promoting the Development of Computers', which provides conditional loans for development costs, qualifying as an innovation instrument for firms.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: MITI published a 'Vision' in 1970 highlighting the importance of knowledge-intensive industries, with particular emphasis on coordinating plans for computers and integrated circuits as part of a broader industrial development strategy.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Strategic policy vision identifying knowledge-intensive industries as priorities for development, providing direction for sectoral R&D investment and industrial coordination.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: Text states MITI published the Vision in 1970.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: Policy vision document establishing strategic direction; important for framing but not itself a direct funding or implementation mechanism.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The 'Vision' published by MITI in 1970 highlighted the importance of knowledge-intensive industries. In particular, plans for computers and integrated circuits were closely tied together.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The 'Vision' published by MITI discusses the importance of knowledge-intensive industries but does not indicate any specific R&D funding or knowledge transfer mechanisms.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Japan's public R&D subsidies are directed mainly towards low-technology industries such as clothing and footwear, where the small scale and limited profitability of firms constrains investment in developing new technologies.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Subsidies to low-technology, low-profitability sectors may support short-term employment and firm viability but risk allocative inefficiency by directing public R&D resources away from higher-productivity, knowledge-intensive sectors where spillovers and growth potential are greater.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: Text uses present tense ('are directed') indicating ongoing practice at time of survey (1985).
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: Descriptive observation of subsidy allocation pattern; not a new reform but rather a characterization of existing subsidy distribution.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: In marked contrast to other OECD countries, public R&D subsidies in Japan go mainly to such low-technology industries as clothing or footwear, where the small scale and limited profitability of firms constrains investment in developing new technologies.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The focus on public R&D subsidies directed towards low-technology industries does not align with the criteria for inclusion, as it does not promote R&D in high-tech or innovative sectors.
